   545	          (fun haS => ha (hS j haS))
   546	      have hhead :
   547	          condLinearHeadSum t
   548	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x) = ∑ j, y j := by
   549	        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   550	        intro j _
   551	        change (t j).headLinear
   552	            (coordinateRestriction (S j)
   553	              (coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ.biUnion S) x)) =
   554	          (t j).headLinear (coordinateRestriction (S j) x)
   555	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction
   556	          (Finset.subset_biUnion_of_mem S (Finset.mem_univ j))]
   557	      have hselect (j : J) : coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i) = y j :=
   558	        coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint y hy j
   559	      have htail (j : J) :
   560	          CondLinearTerm.supportedOn ((t j).tail (y j)) (V j \ S j) := by
   561	        exact CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_tail (ht j) (y j)
   562	      have hDisjointTail : ∀ i j, i ≠ j →
   563	          Disjoint (V i \ S i) (V j \ S j) := by
   564	        intro i j hij
   565	        exact (hDisjoint i j hij).mono Finset.sdiff_subset Finset.sdiff_subset
   566	      have htail_eval (j : J) :
   567	          CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   568	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) =
   569	            CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   570	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   571	        have hrestrict := CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction
   572	          (htail j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   573	        rwa [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction Finset.sdiff_subset] at hrestrict
   574	      have hcomponent (j : J) :
   575	          CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) =
   576	            y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   577	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by
   578	        rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_succ_eq]
   579	        change (t j).headLinear
   580	              (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) +
   581	            CondLinearTerm.eval
   582	              ((t j).tail
   583	                ((t j).headLinear
   584	                  (coordinateRestriction (S j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x))))
   585	              (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   586	        rw [coordinateRestriction_coordinateRestriction (hS j)]
   587	        change y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   588	            (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) = _
   589	        rw [htail_eval]
   590	      have hrec := ih (fun j => V j \ S j) hDisjointTail
   591	        (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) htail x
   592	      have htail_family :
   593	          (fun j => (t j).tail (coordinateRestriction (V j) (∑ i, y i))) =
   594	            (fun j => (t j).tail (y j)) := by
   595	        funext j
   596	        rw [hselect]
   597	      calc
   598	        CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.directSum V (ell + 1) t) x =
   599	            (∑ j, y j) +
   600	              CondLinearTerm.eval
   601	                (CondLinearTerm.directSum (fun j => V j \ S j) ell
   602	                  (fun j => (t j).tail (y j))) x := by
   603	              change condLinearHeadSum t
   604	                    (coordinateRestriction
   605	                      (Finset.univ.biUnion fun j => (t j).headSupport) x) +
   606	                  CondLinearTerm.eval
   607	                    (CondLinearTerm.directSum
   608	                      (fun j => V j \ (t j).headSupport) ell
   609	                      (fun j => (t j).tail
   610	                        (coordinateRestriction (V j)
   611	                          (condLinearHeadSum t
   612	                            (coordinateRestriction
   613	                              (Finset.univ.biUnion fun i => (t i).headSupport) x))))) x = _
   614	              rw [show (fun j => (t j).headSupport) = S from rfl, hhead]
   615	              rw [htail_family]
   616	        _ = (∑ j, y j) + ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   617	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x) := by rw [hrec]
   618	        _ = ∑ j, (y j + CondLinearTerm.eval ((t j).tail (y j))
   619	              (coordinateRestriction (V j \ S j) x)) := Finset.sum_add_distrib.symm
   620	        _ = ∑ j, CondLinearTerm.eval (t j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x) := by
   621	              apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   622	              intro j _
   623	              exact (hcomponent j).symm
   624	
   625	/-- Equal-level direct sums of maps on disjoint registers are conditionally
   626	linear on the union of those registers.  This is a formalization-only
   627	auxiliary for `lem:cl-func-prod`, blueprint
   628	`lem:cl-func-prod-same-level`. -/
   629	theorem IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   630	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   631	    (V : J → Finset ι) (ell : ℕ) (L : J → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   632	    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   633	    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) ell (L j)) :
   634	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ.biUnion V) ell
   635	      (fun x => ∑ j, L j (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)) := by
   636	  classical
   637	  choose t ht ht_eval using hL
   638	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.directSum V ell t,
   639	    CondLinearTerm.directSum_supportedOn V hDisjoint ell t ht, ?_⟩
   640	  funext x
   641	  rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_directSum V hDisjoint ell t ht x]
   642	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   643	  intro j _
   644	  exact congrFun (ht_eval j) (coordinateRestriction (V j) x)
   645	
   646	/--
   647	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   648	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   649	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   650	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   651	-/
   652	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   653	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   654	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   655	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   656	
   657	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   658	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   659	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   660	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   661	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   662	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   663	-/
   664	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   665	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   666	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   667	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   668	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   669	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   670	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   671	
   672	/--
   673	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   674	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:548-559`, with
   675	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:282-314`.
   676	The map `condLinearConcat` realizes this concatenation on the direct sum.
   677	-/
   678	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   679	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   680	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   681	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   682	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   683	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   684	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   685	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   686	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   687	  classical
   688	  rcases hL with ⟨tL, htL, htL_eval⟩
   689	  let rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell := fun u =>
   690	    if hu : u ∈ Set.range L then Classical.choose (hR u hu)
   691	    else CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel ell
   692	  have hr_supported (u : ιU → K) :
   693	      CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rTerm u) (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) := by
   694	    by_cases hu : u ∈ Set.range L
   695	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   696	      exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).1
   697	    · simp only [rTerm, dif_neg hu]
   698	      exact CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn ell Finset.univ
   699	  have hr_eval (u : ιU → K) (hu : u ∈ Set.range L) :
   700	      CondLinearTerm.eval (rTerm u) = R u := by
   701	    simp only [rTerm, dif_pos hu]
   702	    exact (Classical.choose_spec (hR u hu)).2
   703	  rw [Nat.add_comm k ell]
   704	  refine ⟨CondLinearTerm.concat rTerm 0 tL, ?_, ?_⟩
   705	  · have hsupport := CondLinearTerm.concat_supportedOn
   706	      (acc := (0 : ιU → K)) htL hr_supported
   707	    have huniv :
   708	        (Finset.univ : Finset ιU).map Function.Embedding.inl ∪
   709	            (Finset.univ : Finset ιV).map Function.Embedding.inr =
   710	          (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) := by
   711	      ext i
   712	      cases i <;> simp
   713	    simpa only [huniv] using hsupport
   714	  · funext x
   715	    rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_concat]
   716	    simp only [zero_add]
   717	    rw [congrFun htL_eval (fun i => x (.inl i))]
   718	    rw [hr_eval (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) ⟨_, rfl⟩]
   719	    rfl
   720	
   721	/--
   722	The graph distribution is uniform on ordered pairs `(a, b)` whose unordered
   723	pair belongs to `E`, including self-loops.  This is `def:graph-distribution`
   724	in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:679-691`;
   725	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   726	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   727	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   728	-/
   729	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   730	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   731	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   732	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   733	
   734	/-- The graph distribution has total mass one whenever its edge set is
   735	nonempty.  This is `lem:graph-distribution-mass` in
   736	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:693-698`. -/
   737	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   738	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   739	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   740	  apply Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability
   741	  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := hE
   742	  obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, rfl⟩ := Sym2.mk_surjective e
   743	  change s(a, b) ∈ E at he
   744	  exact ⟨(a, b), Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, he⟩⟩
   745	
   746	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    23	/-- Add one empty first stage to a representation of a conditionally linear
    24	function. -/
    25	private def CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    26	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    27	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) :=
    28	  .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => t)

    30	@[simp]
    31	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    32	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    33	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
    34	    CondLinearTerm.eval t.raiseLevel x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
    35	  simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval]

    37	private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    38	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    39	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    40	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
    41	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t.raiseLevel S := by
    42	  exact ⟨Finset.empty_subset S, fun _ => by simpa using ht⟩

    44	/-- Raise a representation of a conditionally linear function by a specified
    45	number of empty stages. -/
    46	private def CondLinearTerm.raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    47	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    48	    (d : ℕ) → {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell →
    49	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + d)
    50	  | 0, _, t => t
    51	  | d + 1, _, t => (raiseBy d t).raiseLevel

    53	@[simp]
    54	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    55	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
    56	    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
    57	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
    58	  induction d with
    59	  | zero => rfl
    60	  | succ d ih => simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseBy, ih]

    62	private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    63	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
    64	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    65	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
    66	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) S := by
    67	  induction d with
    68	  | zero => exact ht
    69	  | succ d ih => exact CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn ih

    71	/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
    72	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    73	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
    74	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    75	    (h : ell ≤ k) : IsCondLinearOn K S k L := by
    76	  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
    77	  have hk : ell + (k - ell) = k := Nat.add_sub_of_le h
    78	  rw [← hk]
    79	  exact ⟨CondLinearTerm.raiseBy (k - ell) t,
    80	    CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn _ ht,
    81	    funext fun x => by rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy, congrFun ht_eval x]⟩

    83	/-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` has values supported on `S`. -/
    84	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    85	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
    86	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    87	    (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) : L x a = 0 := by
    88	  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
    89	  rw [← congrFun (congrFun ht_eval x) a]
    90	  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem ht x ha

    92	/-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` depends only on the input in

    94	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_coordinateRestriction {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    95	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
    96	    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    97	    (x : ι → K) : L (coordinateRestriction S x) = L x := by
    98	  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
    99	  rw [← congrFun ht_eval, CondLinearTerm.eval_coordinateRestriction ht,
   100	    congrFun ht_eval]

   102	/-- Prepend one supported linear stage to a family of residual
   103	conditionally-linear maps. -/
   104	private theorem IsCondLinearOn.cons {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   105	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S S₁ : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
   106	    (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   107	    (hS₁ : S₁ ⊆ S) (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
   108	    (R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   109	    (hR : ∀ y, IsCondLinearOn K (S \ S₁) ell (R y)) :
   110	    IsCondLinearOn K S (ell + 1) (fun x =>
   111	      L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
   112	        R (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) x) := by
   113	  classical
   114	  choose t ht ht_eval using hR
   115	  refine ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport t, ⟨hS₁, ht⟩, ?_⟩
   116	  funext x
   117	  change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
   118	      CondLinearTerm.eval (t (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _
   119	  rw [congrFun (ht_eval _) x]

   121	private theorem coordinateRestriction_eq_self {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   122	    [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {x : ι → K}
   123	    (hx : ∀ a, a ∉ S → x a = 0) : coordinateRestriction S x = x := by
   124	  ext a
   125	  by_cases ha : a ∈ S
   126	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]
   127	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hx a ha]

   129	private theorem coordinateRestriction_add {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   130	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (x y : ι → K) :
   131	    coordinateRestriction S (x + y) =
   132	      coordinateRestriction S x + coordinateRestriction S y := by
   133	  ext a
   134	  by_cases ha : a ∈ S <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

   136	private theorem coordinateRestriction_eq_zero_of_disjoint {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   137	    [DecidableEq ι] {S T : Finset ι} (hST : Disjoint S T)
   138	    {x : ι → K} (hx : ∀ a, a ∉ T → x a = 0) :
   139	    coordinateRestriction S x = 0 := by
   140	  ext a
   141	  by_cases ha : a ∈ S
   142	  · have haT : a ∉ T := fun h => Finset.disjoint_left.mp hST ha h
   143	    simp [coordinateRestriction, ha, hx a haT]
   144	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

   146	/-- Coordinate restriction as a linear endomorphism. -/
   147	private def coordinateRestrictionLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   148	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) :
   149	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   150	  toFun := coordinateRestriction S
   151	  map_add' := coordinateRestriction_add S
   152	  map_smul' c x := by
   153	    ext a
   154	    by_cases ha : a ∈ S <;> simp [coordinateRestriction, ha]

   156	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   157	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   158	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   159	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) :
   160	    ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x = x := by
   161	  classical
   162	  ext a
   163	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   164	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   165	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   166	  · intro i _ hij
   167	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   168	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   169	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   170	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   171	
   172	private theorem sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   173	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   174	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   175	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (f : J → ι → K)
   176	    (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (x : ι → K) :
   177	    (∑ j, f j) = x ↔ ∀ j, f j = coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   178	  classical
   179	  constructor
   180	  · intro h j
   181	    rw [← h]
   182	    exact (coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint f hf j).symm
   183	  · intro h
   184	    calc
   185	      (∑ j, f j) = ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   186	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => h j
   187	      _ = x := sum_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover x

     4	# Uniform subset estimates
     5	
     6	This file contains estimates for the total variation distance between the
     7	uniform distribution on a finite type and the uniform distribution on a
     8	nonempty finite subset, together with averaging bounds for `[0,1]`-valued
     9	functions.  The uniform-subset total-variation identity is proved by transport
    10	through Mathlib probability mass functions.

    17	/-- Total variation between the uniform distribution on a finite ambient type and
    18	the uniform distribution on a nonempty finite subset.
    19	
    20	This is the elementary finite identity
    21	`TV(uniform α, uniform s) = 1 - |s| / |α|`.  The proof transports the project
    22	`Distribution` statement to Mathlib's uniform probability mass functions. -/
    23	theorem totalVariationDistance_uniformDistribution_uniformOnFinset_eq
    24	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    25	    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    26	    totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) =
    27	      1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
    28	  rw [totalVariationDistance_eq_toPMF_sum]
    29	  change PMF.totalVariationDistance
    30	      ((uniformDistribution α).toPMF (uniformDistribution_isProbability α))
    31	      ((Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).toPMF
    32	        (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)) =
    33	    1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error)
    34	  rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF]
    35	  exact PMF.totalVariationDistance_uniformOfFintype_uniformOfFinset_eq s hs
    36	
    37	/-- A `[0,1]`-valued function averaged over a nonempty finite subset is bounded
    38	by its ambient uniform average plus the total variation distance between the
    39	two uniform distributions. -/

    41	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    42	    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty)
    43	    (f : α → Error)
    44	    (hf_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a)
    45	    (hf_le_one : ∀ a, f a ≤ 1) :

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    14	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
    15	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
    16	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	
    25	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    26	
    27	/--
    28	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    29	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    30	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    31	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    32	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    33	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    34	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    35	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    36	-/
    37	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    38	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    39	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    40	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    41	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    42	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    43	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    44	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    45	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    46	
    47	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    48	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    49	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    51	-/
    52	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    53	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    54	
    55	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    56	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    58	-/
    59	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    60	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    61	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    62	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    63	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    64	      fun x =>
    65	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    66	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    67	
    68	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    69	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    72	-/
    73	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    74	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    75	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    76	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    77	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    78	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    79	
    80	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    81	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    82	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    84	-/
    85	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    86	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    87	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    88	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    89	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    90	
    91	/--
    92	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    93	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    95	-/
    96	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    97	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
    98	
    99	/--
   100	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   101	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   102	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   104	-/
   105	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   106	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   107	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   108	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   109	
   110	/-- The direct-sum map used to encode the paper's CL concatenation.  The left
   111	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member
   112	`R u v` selected by the left input `u`.  This is Lean-only coordinate
   113	infrastructure for `lem:cl-concat`, blueprint
   114	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, paper origin
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   116	-/
   117	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   118	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   119	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   120	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   121	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)
   122	  let v : ιV → K := fun j => x (.inr j)
   123	  Sum.elim (L u) (R (L u) v)
   124	
   125	/--
   126	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is
   127	`lem:cl-concat` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:498-505`, with
   128	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   129	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the
   130	level proof remains deferred in this skeleton.
   131	-/
   132	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   133	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] {ell k : ℕ}
   134	    {L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K)}
   135	    {R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K)}
   136	    (hL : IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιU) k L)
   137	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →
   138	      IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset ιV) ell (R u)) :
   139	    IsCondLinearOn K (Finset.univ : Finset (ιU ⊕ ιV)) (k + ell)
   140	      (condLinearConcat L R) := by
   141	  sorry
   142	
   143	/--
   144	The graph distribution samples an ordered endpoint pair whose unordered edge
   145	`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
   146	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
   147	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
   148	The underlying graph-distribution definition is
   149	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
   150	-/
   151	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   152	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   153	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
   154	    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
   155	
   156	/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
   157	theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   158	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
   159	    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
   160	  sorry
   161	
   162	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-! # Structure and direct sums of conditionally linear functions
     4	
     5	This module records the prefix decomposition of a conditionally linear map and
     6	the behavior of such maps and their shared-seed distributions under finite
     7	coordinate direct sums.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source results are `lem:cl-kth`, `lem:cl-func-prod`, and
    12	`lem:cl-dist-prod` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-587`, with
    13	paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-379`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- The value of the strict-prefix marginal preceding `k`. This is a
    24	formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-kth`, blueprint
    25	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`, paper
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
    27	def clPrefix {K ι : Type*} [Zero K] {ell : ℕ}
    28	    (marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (k : Fin ell)
    29	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    30	  if _hk : k.val = 0 then 0
    31	  else marginal ⟨k.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) k.isLt⟩ x
    32	
    33	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
    34	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
    35	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:520-540`, paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
    37	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    38	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
    39	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
    40	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    41	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
    42	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
    43	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/
    44	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    45	  /-- Each marginal has the corresponding conditionally linear level. -/
    46	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
    47	  /-- The selected factor registers are pairwise disjoint. -/
    48	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →
    49	    Disjoint (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) (factor j (clPrefix marginal j x))

     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.

    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution

   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm

   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- A probability distribution has total weight one over any finite superset
   127	of its explicit support. -/
   128	theorem weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset {α : Type*}
   129	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {s : Finset α}
   130	    (hsubset : 𝒟.support ⊆ s) :
   131	    ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   132	  have hsum :
   133	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a :=
   134	    Finset.sum_subset hsubset (fun a _ ha => 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha)
   135	  exact hsum ▸ h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   136	
   137	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   138	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.
   139	
   140	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   141	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   142	than over a stored support finset. -/
   143	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   144	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   145	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   146	  simpa using h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   147	
   148	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   149	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   150	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   151	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   152	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   153	
   154	/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
   155	theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   156	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   157	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
   158	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟
   159	
   160	end Distribution.IsProbability

   164	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`

   166	
   167	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by

   171	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=

   176	      simp)
   177	    (by
   178	      intro a ha
   179	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   180	      simp)

namespace Distribution

/-- The uniform distribution on a specified finite support.

The stored support is `s`, and the weight of a point is the elementary finite
uniform weight `1 / s.card` on `s` and `0` off `s`.  When the support is empty
this gives the zero sub-probability distribution, matching the convention used
for degenerate filtered supports in the LDT development. -/
noncomputable def uniformOnFinset {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) : Distribution α :=
  letI := Classical.decEq α
  { support := s
    weight := fun a => if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0
    nonnegative := fun _ => by
      split_ifs <;> positivity
    outsideSupport := fun _ ha => by
      simp [ha] }

@[simp]
theorem uniformOnFinset_support {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) :
    (uniformOnFinset s).support = s := rfl

@[simp]
theorem uniformOnFinset_weight {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (s : Finset α) (a : α) :
    (uniformOnFinset s).weight a =
      if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0 := by
  by_cases ha : a ∈ s
  · simp [uniformOnFinset, ha]
  · simp [uniformOnFinset, ha]

/-- A nonempty finite support gives a probability distribution. -/
theorem uniformOnFinset_isProbability {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    (uniformOnFinset s).IsProbability := by
  classical
  dsimp [IsProbability, totalWeight]
  simp_rw [uniformOnFinset_weight]
  have hcard_nat : s.card ≠ 0 := Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr hs
  have hcard : (s.card : Error) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast hcard_nat
  have hsum :
      (∑ a ∈ s, if a ∈ s then 1 / (s.card : Error) else 0) =
        ∑ _a ∈ s, 1 / (s.card : Error) := by
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro a ha
    simp [ha]
  rw [hsum]
  simp [Finset.sum_const, hcard]

/-- The uniform distribution on any finite support is a sub-probability
distribution.  It has mass `1` on nonempty support and mass `0` on empty
support. -/
theorem uniformOnFinset_weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformOnFinset s).support, (uniformOnFinset s).weight a ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  by_cases hs : s.Nonempty
  · exact (uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs).weight_sum_le_one
  · have hsempty : s = ∅ := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hs
    simp [hsempty]

/-- The project uniform distribution on a nonempty finite support is Mathlib's
uniform probability mass function on that support. -/
theorem uniformOnFinset_toPMF
    {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    (uniformOnFinset s).toPMF (uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs) =
      PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs := by
  ext a
  rw [toPMF_apply]
  rw [show (uniformOnFinset s).weight a =
      (PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs a).toReal by
        classical
        by_cases ha : a ∈ s
        · simp [uniformOnFinset_weight, PMF.uniformOfFinset_apply, ha,
            ENNReal.toReal_inv, ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
        · simp [uniformOnFinset_weight, PMF.uniformOfFinset_apply, ha]]
  exact ENNReal.ofReal_toReal ((PMF.uniformOfFinset s hs).apply_ne_top a)

end Distribution

/-- The uniform distribution on a nonempty finite type. -/
noncomputable def uniformDistribution (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] : Distribution α :=
  Distribution.uniformOnFinset Finset.univ

/-- The uniform distribution on a finite type has full support. -/
@[simp]
theorem uniformDistribution_support (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :
    (uniformDistribution α).support = Finset.univ := rfl

/-- The weights of a uniform distribution sum to exactly `1`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_weight_sum_eq_one (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 := by
  have h : (uniformDistribution α).IsProbability := by
    simpa [uniformDistribution] using
      Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability (Finset.univ : Finset α)
        Finset.univ_nonempty
  exact h.weight_sum_eq_one

/-- The uniform distribution is a genuine probability distribution. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_isProbability (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :
    (uniformDistribution α).IsProbability := by
  simpa [uniformDistribution] using
    Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability (Finset.univ : Finset α) Finset.univ_nonempty

/-- The weights of a uniform distribution sum to at most `1`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_weight_sum_le_one (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :
    ∑ a ∈ (uniformDistribution α).support, (uniformDistribution α).weight a ≤ 1 :=
  le_of_eq (uniformDistribution_weight_sum_eq_one α)

/-- The project uniform distribution on a nonempty finite type is Mathlib's
uniform probability mass function on that type. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_toPMF
    (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] :
    (uniformDistribution α).toPMF (uniformDistribution_isProbability α) =
      PMF.uniformOfFintype α := by
  simpa [uniformDistribution, PMF.uniformOfFintype] using
    Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF (Finset.univ : Finset α) Finset.univ_nonempty

## Pattern 3: Split-module architecture

### Directory structure

The Lean codebase is organized into per-chapter subdirectories under
`MIPStarRE/LDT/`, each with its own internal structure:

```
MIPStarRE/LDT/
├── Basic/                    # Parameters, operators, submeasurements, distributions
├── Test/                     # Test definitions, main theorem, error cascade
├── Preliminaries/            # Polynomials, finite fields, Cauchy–Schwarz, Fourier
├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/   # Orthonormalization, projective completion
├── MainInductionStep/        # Section 6 induction theorem
├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/  # Section 7–8 expansion, global variance
├── GlobalVariance/           # Section 8.5 (and related global variance machinery)
├── SelfImprovement/          # Section 9 self-improvement
├── CommutativityPoints/      # Section 10 commutativity setup
├── Tactic/                   # Section 10 proof orchestration utilities
├── Commutativity/            # Section 11 commutativity bounds
└── Pasting/                  # Section 12 pasting
```

### Subdirectory layout convention

Each subdirectory follows a consistent internal layout:

```
SubModule/
├── Defs.lean        # New structures, type abbreviations, error-term definitions
├── Statements.lean   # Statement-level types (hypothesis bundles, conclusion shapes)
├── Theorems.lean     # Public re-export, when the section has one
└── Theorems/
    ├── Core.lean     # Main proof of the chapter's theorem
    ├── ...           # Supporting proof leaves
    └── Results.lean  # Re-export file for the proof leaves
```

Some larger chapters (like `Pasting/` and `SelfImprovement/`) have more
internal subdivisions (e.g., `Pasting/Bernoulli/`, `Pasting/Sandwich/`,
`SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/`).  When an outer `Theorems.lean` module is
present, it imports the public proof leaves.

### Why split instead of monolithic files?

| Reason | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Compilation parallelism** | Lean's per-file compilation is single-threaded per file; smaller files mean faster individual type-checking loops |
| **Dependency isolation** | A proof leaf in `Pasting/Sandwich/` only depends on `Pasting/Defs.lean` and `Pasting/Statements.lean`, not on the entire pasting proof chain |
| **Edit locality** | Changing a helper in `SelfImprovement/Theorems/Results/AddInUStep12/Raw.lean` does not re-elaborate unrelated downstream leaves unless the helper's type changed |
| **Reviewability** | A 200-line proof leaf is easier to review than a 4000-line monolithic proof block |
| **Parallel agent work** | Different agents can work on different proof leaves concurrently without merge conflicts |

### When *not* to split further

Don't split a file just to have one theorem per file.  A single file
containing 3–5 related lemmas that share helper definitions and proof
structure is better than 5 files each with one lemma and duplicate
helper material.

When splitting does happen, the new leaves, declarations, and module
names must follow the mathematical naming norm in
`docs/mathematical_language.md`: name the mathematical boundary, not
the paper line number, workflow step, or implementation phase.

### Re-export files

See [Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern](#pattern-4-public-re-export-pattern)
below.

---

## Pattern 4: Public re-export pattern

Public subdirectories with several proof leaves may have a root-level
re-export file that imports the source-facing leaves.  For example, the
top-level LDT module imports the public section APIs:

```lean
import MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.ProjectivizationChain.Output
import MIPStarRE.LDT.MainInductionStep.Theorems.MainTheorems.Successor
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Pasting.Bernoulli.Final
```

The re-export module itself contains no new mathematical declarations. It is a
public import convenience.  When no such public module exists, downstream code
should import the specific leaf module whose declarations it uses.

The top-level re-export file is `MIPStarRE.lean`, which imports all
subdirectories.  `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean` imports all LDT subdirectories.

**When to add to a re-export file**: When a new proof leaf is added to a
public theorem or definition subdirectory and the leaf is part of the intended
section-level API, add its import to the relevant public module.

**When not to add**: If a leaf is only used by one other leaf (internal
helper), do not add it to a public re-export module; let the consumer import it
directly so its API surface does not leak.

## Reviewer checklist

Use this alongside the blocker
list in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)
checklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper
result, ask:

- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the
      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.
- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If
      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match
      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.
- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if
      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature
      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.
- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an
      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness
      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.
- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a
      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it
      (A5).
- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /
      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its
      grounding plan (A6)?
- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's
      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences
      as ⚠️S in [#1379].

A lemma that passes all of these is a proof. A lemma that fails one is
scaffolding, and should be labelled and tracked as such (don't tag with
`\leanok` until the gap is closed).

## CI prevention

Mechanical detection is possible for many of these patterns:

- **A1 (conclusion-shaped hypothesis).** Use
  `python3 scripts/audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci` as the current
  report-only tripwire for the PR [#491] inline-existential mutation. It parses
  theorem/lemma headers and warns when an explicit existential hypothesis shares
  the conclusion's salient structure, while printing witness-adapter helpers
  separately. When [#438] lands (`\leanok` ↔ `sorryAx` drift), extend the same
  idea to all `\leanok`-tagged declarations: parse the hypothesis list; if any
  hypothesis's type (modulo `∃`/`∀`/`∧`) contains a prefix of the conclusion
  structure, warn.
- **A2 (definitional sleight).** Grep for `theorem <Name>.* := rfl` where
  `<Name>` has a blueprint `\lean{}` cross-reference. The only allowed cases
  are ones annotated with `@[paper_bookkeeping]` (proposed attribute) or in
  an allow-list.
- **A3 (zero-fallback).** Grep for identifier suffixes `fallback`, `or0`,
  `orDefault`, `placeholder`, `sentinel` in `Defs/*` files. Each should have
  a docstring citing the downstream eligibility precondition.
